explanation: W = 1.45 GeV is below the ep -> e'p(eta) production threshold. The threshold is W_thr = m_p + m_eta = 0.938272 GeV + 0.547862 GeV = 1.486134 GeV, so at W = 1.45 GeV there is not enough energy in the hadronic system to produce a proton plus an eta meson at rest; this kinematic point does not exist physically. This was independently confirmed by running the eta-configured EXCLURAD executable (build/exclurad) on the requested point: it read the EtaMAID-2023 table (maid07-PPpi.tbl) and printed the valid W range as W min = 1.4856 GeV, W max = 6.0 GeV (the tabulated grid begins essentially at the eta threshold), i.e. v2 = 1.45 falls outside [W min, W max]. The run exited normally but produced no radiative-correction output: radcor.dat, radtot.dat, radsigpl.dat, radsigmi.dat, and radasm.dat were all empty, and all.dat contained only the header/run-configuration block with no computed cross sections, delta, or sigma_born. No physically meaningful delta could be produced for this request; delta and sigma_born are reported as null. To get a valid result, choose W >= 1.4856 GeV (e.g. W = 1.5 GeV) at the same Q2, cos(theta*), and phi*.
